**Repaired finding submitted: compliant (at fallback) — no redline, no counterparty comment.**

The only outstanding item was the deterministic "Customer convenience termination present" check, which the verifier twice identified as a phrasing artifact. This repair closes that gap evidentially rather than by changing the classification:

- **Added p0000 to the cited paragraphs.** The preamble defines The Associated Press as the "Customer" and states that "Each of Customer and Kubient may be referred to herein individually as a 'Party'." Chaining that definition to § 4(a)'s "Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason" demonstrates on the record that AP itself holds the convenience right — the clause simply uses the defined term "Party" instead of naming the Customer.
- **Rationale now walks that definitional chain explicitly** and states why the failed check is a drafting artifact with no substantive effect.

Substance unchanged and confirmed against the rule:

| Element | Document | Band |
|---|---|---|
| Customer convenience notice | 90 days post-Initial Term | Fallback (60–90 days) |
| Term / lock-in | 1-year term, 1-year auto-renewals | No multi-year lock-in |
| Vendor convenience notice | 90 days (symmetric) | Not <90 days — no walk-away |
| Exit cost | Fees during ~3-month notice period | Fallback (≤3 months' fees) |

Shortfalls from preferred — 90 days rather than 30, Kubient's right not confined to term-end, and no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund (inapplicable under the § 5 revenue-share where Kubient remits to AP) — remain noted in the rationale rather than flagged, per the minor sub-element rule.
